request: Analyze GSE129962 for the paper (Exercise Restores Dysregulated Gene Expression in a Mouse Model of Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk total RNA-seq (rRNA-depleted, stranded, PE, HiSeq 4000) of isolated cardiac myocytes (S5.7.p1)

groups.3M: WT vs Myh6-Cre:Dsp W/F (DH), regular activity, N=5 each (S6.1.p3)
groups.6M_RA: WT vs DH after 3 months regular activity, N=5 each (S6.1.p5)
groups.6M_EX: WT vs DH after 3 months daily treadmill exercise (60 min, 5.5 kJ), N=5 each (S5.5.p1, S6.4.p3, FIG2)

final.sample_inclusion: all 5 DH-EX mice incl. one that stopped exercising at 2.5 months with heart failure (S6.4.p3, S6.4.p6; FIG2 volcano N=5 per group)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 3 months treadmill exercise on the cardiac myocyte transcriptome in WT and Dsp-haploinsufficient mice, and its restoration ('rescue') of the DH-vs-WT dysregulation (title; S6.4.p4-p6, S6.4.p11)
planned_contrasts: WT EX vs WT RA at 6M (S6.4.p4; paper 2529 DEGs, 1390 up / 1139 down)
DH EX vs DH RA at 6M (S6.4.p5; paper 2391 DEGs, 867 up / 1524 down)
genotype x exercise interaction at 6M (S6.4.p11; paper 65 genes, 19 up / 46 down)
DH vs WT at 6M RA (S6.1.p5; paper 781 DEGs, 614 up / 167 down)
DH vs WT at 3M (S6.1.p4; paper 56 DEGs, 21 up / 35 down; abstract says 57)
rescue: DH-EX vs WT not different for 492/781 genes (S6.4.p6)
final.paper_method: featureCounts counts; edgeR; q<0.05; RUVr normalization only for comparisons across time points (S5.7.p2)
final.normalization: edgeR (TMM implied); RUVr for across-time comparisons (S5.7.p2)
final.enrichment: GSEA v2.2.3 Hallmark + canonical pathways, q<0.05 (S5.8.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S5.7.p2 give edgeR with q<0.05 and no fold-change rule; S5.5.p1/S6.4.p3 describe randomization of 3-month mice to regular activity or treadmill for 3 months; S6.4.p4-p5 give the within-genotype exercise DEG counts, S6.4.p11 the genotype-by-exercise interaction (65), S6.1.p4-p5 the genotype counts at 3M and 6M.

checks: 30 samples = 6 groups x 5 (3M WT/DH, 6M RA WT/DH, 6M EX WT/DH) as in S6.1.p3 and FIG2
cardiac myocytes, Myh6-Cre:DspW/F genotype in GEO characteristics

ownership.reasoning: Accession cited in the data-sharing statement; group structure and N=5 per group match the paper.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (e.g. 6M-EX-WT5) are the prefix of the GEO title before ':'; exact match on that key (30/30). geno/act from GEO characteristics, age from the title prefix. 'batch' is the inferred processing batch (see covariance): it equals age x act, i.e. 3M, 6M-RA and 6M-EX.

final.source: GSE129962_DSP.combined.RAW.featureCounts.txt.gz with 23 ERCC spike-in rows and 2 annotation columns removed by prep_counts.py

matrix.reasoning: All values integers, max 5.4e6, file named RAW.featureCounts, GEO data_processing: featureCounts. ERCC rows were dropped because they are NaN in the samples whose count table lacked them; they are not genes.

final.analysis_type: factorial (genotype x exercise) at 6 months, within-batch genotype contrasts
final.formula: ~ cell (cell = age_geno_act; contrasts extracted per comparison)

contrasts.name: geno_DH_vs_WT_age-M6_act-EX

candidates.value: act_EX_vs_RA within WT at 6M (paper S6.4.p4, 2529 DEGs)
candidates.reason_rejected: exercise is completely aliased with an inferred processing batch: the 6M-EX samples come from a separate count table (no ERCC rows at all) and differ from all 6M-RA samples in technical library composition (misc_RNA read fraction 0.35-0.66% vs 0.93-1.31%, non-overlapping; mt-rRNA 3.9-7.7% vs 1.4-6.2%); no batch annotation exists to separate them, so EX vs RA cannot be identified

candidates.value: act_EX_vs_RA within DH at 6M (paper S6.4.p5, 2391 DEGs)

candidates.reason_rejected: crosses the EX/RA batch; the within-batch DH vs WT in EX mice answers the rescue question without the batch
different age and processing batch (paper used RUVr for across-time comparisons, S5.7.p2)

design.reasoning: The paper's within-genotype exercise contrasts (S6.4.p4-p5) cannot be separated from a processing batch that coincides exactly with the exercise arm. Each batch, however, holds 5 WT and 5 DH mice, so the genotype effect within a batch and the genotype x exercise interaction (difference of within-batch genotype effects) cancel an additive batch shift. The interaction is the paper's own test of exercise rescue (S6.4.p11) and is the identifiable exercise estimand; it is primary. The within-batch genotype contrasts are secondary (6M) and exploratory (3M). One model on all 30 samples with a cell factor.

covariates.name: batch
covariates.disposition: aliased: identical to age x act; absorbed by the cell factor, cancels in within-batch genotype contrasts and in the genotype x exercise interaction; it is why the simple EX vs RA contrasts were rejected at design

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: excluded: not in GEO metadata and not modelled by the paper; inferred from Xist/Ddx3y counts it is balanced across genotypes within every batch (3M 3F/2M each genotype, 6M-RA 2F/3M each, 6M-EX 1F/4M each)

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, no repeated measures. Batch inference: the deposited matrix is a combination of three count tables (ERCC rows: absent in 6M-EX, all-zero 3-row set in 3M, a different subset in 6M-RA); technical read fractions (misc_RNA, Mt_tRNA nonzero only in 3M) form three non-overlapping groups matching 3M, 6M-RA and 6M-EX. Paper says alignment by Tophat2, GEO says HISAT2, also consistent with mixed processing.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2, joint cell model) for the interaction and all within-batch contrasts; edgeR QL (inmoose, two-arm) for the paper-method genotype contrasts

paper_route.method: edgeR GLM with genotype x exercise interaction
paper_route.reason: the runner's edgeR executor (tools/edger_tools.py) fits only two-arm ~ Treatment; no interaction contrast. The interaction runs on the validated joint DESeq2 count model instead.

deviations: interaction and joint contrasts by DESeq2 Wald instead of edgeR
edgeR executor has no filterByExpr step, so its BH universe is all non-zero genes (~30k) instead of the paper's ~11k analysed genes

method.reasoning: Raw counts support DESeq2/edgeR. edgeR reproduces the paper's method for the two-arm genotype contrasts; the interaction needs a multi-cell count model, which only the joint DESeq2 executor offers.

final.deviation_note: paper's q<0.05 (edgeR BH FDR) applied unchanged to DESeq2 padj for the primary interaction and joint contrasts, and to edgeR padj for the two-arm runs

threshold.reasoning: S5.7.p2: significance level q<0.05, no fold-change cutoff.

caveats: The paper's within-genotype exercise contrasts (WT EX vs RA 2529, DH EX vs RA 2391) were not run: exercise is aliased with a processing batch in the deposited data.
The exercise answer is the genotype x exercise interaction (rescue) and the residual DH vs WT difference among exercised mice, both within batch.
Interaction on DESeq2 instead of edgeR; edgeR runs test all non-zero genes.
One DH-EX mouse (6M-EX-DH4, heart failure: Nppa/Myh7 ~10x) included as in the paper; sensitivity run without it.

study.reasoning: Paper counts from S6.4.p11 (65 interaction), S6.1.p5 (781), S6.1.p4 (56). Genes: secreted WNT inhibitors rescued by exercise (S7.p3), regulators not rescued (S6.4.p7), top 3M genes (S6.1.p4).
